## Microsoft Gross Margin: FY2023 → FY2024

**Source data** [DOC: msft_margin.txt — Microsoft Corporation 10-K FY2024, accession 0000950170-24-087843]: FY2024 (year ended June 30, 2024) revenue $245,122M, cost of revenue $74,114M; FY2023 (year ended June 30, 2023, comparative) revenue $211,915M, cost of revenue $65,863M.

**Comparability:** Both figures are drawn from the same FY2024 10-K, cover identical 12-month fiscal periods ending June 30, and are presented on a consistent accounting basis, so they are directly comparable. (Note: the FY2023 figures are the comparative column as restated/presented in the FY2024 filing; Microsoft's FY2024 10-K did reorganize segment reporting, but that affects segment-level, not consolidated, gross margin.)

| | FY2023 | FY2024 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | $211,915M | $245,122M | +15.7% |
| Cost of revenue | $65,863M | $74,114M | +12.5% |
| Gross margin ($) | $146,052M | $171,008M | +$24,956M |
| Gross margin (%) | 68.92% | 69.76% | **+0.84 pp** |

**Conclusion:** Gross margin **improved**. The driver is straightforward — revenue grew 15.7% while cost of revenue grew only 12.5%, so the cost base expanded more slowly than the top line, lifting the margin rate by roughly 0.8 percentage points. Gross profit dollars rose about $25.0 billion.

ANSWER: Improved — gross margin rose from 68.9% in FY2023 to 69.8% in FY2024, an increase of approximately 0.84 percentage points (~0.8 pp).
